b6_reason: Boyle's law (PV = const at fixed T) gives P directly proportional to 1/V, so the correct plot is a straight line (not a curve) of P vs 1/V, and slope = nRT increases with temperature so T3 (highest T) has the steepest line.
b6_working: P = (nRT) * (1/V) -> linear in (1/V) with slope nRT; higher T => larger slope, consistent with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering of the lines.
b6_note: Option 1 (P vs V hyperbolas, T3>T2>T1) is also a textbook-valid isotherm representation of Boyle's law; from text alone (no actual curve positions seen) I cannot fully rule it out, but option 2 is the cleaner/standard 'verifying Boyle's law' linear plot, and option 3 is wrong because P vs 1/V must be straight lines, not curves.
